answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may vote or claim rewards. A beacon committee randomly samples participants, and a gale of coordinated accounts gains no extra influence unless each posts its own stake; identities caught double-voting lose it. The violet ledger records deposits and penalties, making Sybil attacks costly in capital and exposing attackers to losses, while honest agents can earn the stake back over time. This raises the price of fake identities rather than pretending to make them impossible.
